item.title: Sunday on 60 Minutes: Trump talks Democrats' sweeping midterm wins
item.description: Watch 60 Minutes on Sunday at 7 p.m. ET/PT on CBS and Paramount+.

item.title: Trump told 60 Minutes to expect post-midterm firings
item.description: President Trump announced that Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff just hours after he told 60 Minutes that he'd be shaking up his team.

item.title: Trump said to expect firings. Hours later, he announced Susie Wiles' departure.
item.description: President Trump hinted at possible firings following Democrats' sweeping midterm wins, telling 60 Minutes' Ross Douthat he plans to make "maybe a few changes" to his Cabinet. Watch more of the interview Sunday only on 60 Minutes.

item.title: These House and Senate midterm races don't have winners yet
item.description: Democrats won sizable House and Senate majorities in the 2026 midterm elections, but the exact margins are unclear because some races haven't been projected yet. Here's where the results stand.

item.title: Lawmakers react with criticism as Trump replaces Wiles with Miller after midterm loss
item.description: President Trump is facing criticism from lawmakers after replacing White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller following a midterm loss that was driven in part by outrage over ICE tactics. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi and Nikole Killion break it down.

item.title: What Trump's choice to replace Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller means
item.description: Marc Caputo, a CBS News contributor and White House reporter for Axios, and Marc Short, a Republican strategist and former chief of staff to Vice President Mike Pence, join "The Takeout" to discuss Stephen Miller's new role as chief of staff.

item.title: White House restores financial disclosure page after CBS News inquiry
item.description: The White House's page listing dozens of financial disclosure forms went offline without explanation, only to be restored after CBS News inquired about its removal.

item.title: Democrats win Senate control — live updates
item.description: Democrats were able to pick up the seats needed to gain control of the Senate, CBS News projects, and the party scored several upset victories in red states.

item.title: Cornell's Faculty Senate votes "no confidence" in administration
item.description: Cornell University's Faculty Senate approved a resolution expressing no confidence in the university's administration, including Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff and other administrators.

item.title: DOJ official resigns amid questions about "grand conspiracy" probe
item.description: Jason Reding Quiñones, U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida, abruptly resigned, marking another high-profile departure from a DOJ inquiry plagued by internal disputes.

item.title: DNC Chair Ken Martin on the midterms, uncalled races
item.description: Ken Martin, chair of the Democratic National Committee, joins "The Takeout" to discuss the party's big wins in the midterms, uncalled races and more.

item.title: Mississippi Senate race still a toss-up; Democrat holds slim lead
item.description: The Senate race in deep-red Mississippi remains unresolved, as Democrat Scott Colom has mounted a surprisingly competitive challenge to incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

item.title: Trump shakes up team as Democratic majority comes into focus
item.description: President Trump is swapping out his chief of staff after Republicans' losses in the midterms, with more than two dozen House races unresolved. Follow live updates.

item.title: Michigan Governor-elect Jocelyn Benson shares her plans for healthcare, more
item.description: Michigan Governor-elect Jocelyn Benson joins "The Takeout" to discuss her plans for the state following a successful midterm election for Democrats.

item.title: The status of uncalled midterm races in Mississippi, Alaska, beyond
item.description: CBS News' director of elections and surveys, Anthony Salvanto, breaks down the status of uncalled midterm races, including Mississippi and Alaska.

item.title: What the White House might look like with Stephen Miller as the new chief of staff
item.description: President Trump is replacing his current chief of staff, Susie Wiles, with immigration enforcement advocate Stephen Miller. CBS News senior White House correspondent Weijia Jiang reports.

item.title: Politicians react to Trump's decision to replace chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller
item.description: Reactions are coming in from Capitol Hill to President Trump's decision to replace White House chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller, who is known for being tough on immigration. CBS News congressional correspondent Nikole Killion reports.

item.title: GOP Sen. Ron Johnson on working to delay Congress leadership elections, more
item.description: Republican Sen. Ron Johnson of Wisconsin joins "The Takeout" to discuss President Trump's decision to replace his White House chief of staff, his push to delay the GOP Senate leadership elections, and more.

item.title: Trump touts imminent decision on potential new attack on Iran
item.description: President Trump says he will make a decision soon on whether to order new strikes on Iran, calls Qatari emir as mediators push for a peace deal.

item.title: Stocks rebound after AI selloff that pushed NASDAQ into correction territory
item.description: The stock market saw a rebound on Friday after dipping earlier this week amid AI-related concerns after Democrats won the midterms. Laura Sanicola, a senior writer at Barron's, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Trump installs Stephen Miller as chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
item.description: "I wanted to make a change," President Trump said, explaining the major staffing shakeup.

item.title: Stocks rebound after tech selloff that pushed Nasdaq into correction
item.description: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq edged up in early trading after a Thursday rout driven by concerns about a potential slowdown in data center construction.

item.title: Rob Sand's runway modeling past resurfaces after Iowa gubernatorial win
item.description: Vogue asked on Instagram whether followers knew the Iowa governor-elect once modeled for Prada. A verified account for Sand, who was previously elected to the Iowa state auditor's office, replied affirmatively in the comments.

item.title: Thomas Markle Sr., Meghan's father, arrested in Florida
item.description: It was reported in October that Meghan's estranged father, Thomas Markle, was under investigation by authorities in the Philippines for alleged possession of child sexual abuse materials.

item.title: Data centers are unpopular — and a key motor of economic growth
item.description: The political backlash against data centers is intensifying, threatening to choke off a critical source of U.S. investment, according to economists.

item.title: Pope voted in U.S. election because he's "proud to be an American"
item.description: Pope Leo, who is on a 12-day, three-country trip in Latin America, also said he credits God and doctors for his lung cancer surgery recovery.

item.title: Musk says Tesla will end Cybertruck production next year
item.description: Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the electric car maker will halt production of its Cybertruck next year and prioritize self-driving taxis.

item.title: Exit polls show data centers weren't winners in 2026 elections
item.description: Big majorities of 2026 election voters opposed the building of data centers in their community.

item.title: Newly empowered Democrats could revive plans for court reforms
item.description: Democrats have proposed a variety of measures aimed at reshaping the Supreme Court over the years and may be poised to push them forward after winning House and Senate majorities.

item.title: Feds warn of potential cyberattacks on industrial refrigerators
item.description: After a wave of attacks in Europe, U.S. officials are warning of "ongoing" cyber threats targeting refrigeration systems used in healthcare, agriculture and other industries.
